title: Critical TTFT regression impacting Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — emergency performance hotfix
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden latency regressions (first-token time and tokens/sec) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after runtime-1.21 rolled out two nights ago. Symptoms: elevated TTFT for short prompts (1-3s -> 3-7s), and sustained tokens/sec drop on streaming workloads; observed on both open models and a few quantized variants. Impact: production traffic experienced 10-40% throughput loss and several enterprise customers opened escalations citing SLA breaches and UX regressions. Scope: affects multi-tenant Hosted and Dedicated GPU pools and Private agent nodes running the runtime-1.21 kernel scheduler change. Preliminary hypothesis: the new kernel scheduling optimizer that reorders micro-batches to improve throughput interacts badly with the prefix/KV cache eviction logic for long-lived chat sessions; when a reordered batch hits a stale KV chunk the system falls back to a slow path that serializes KV rewarm, increasing TTFT and reducing tokens/sec. Additionally, a codepath introduced to prefer layered quantized kernels under certain sequence-length distributions appears to have introduced CPU/GPU kernel handshake stalls on some hardware, amplifying the regression.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC — Aisha Kumar: Triage meeting triggered after PagerDuty alert and three customer escalations. Collected initial traces and asked SRE to snapshot affected pods (hosted-prod, dedicated-pool-3, private-customer-12).

2026-03-10 11:05 UTC — Miguel Santos: Reproduced TTFT increase locally on a pinned model using a long multi-turn prompt. Kernel scheduler reorder flag (--enable-microbatch-reorder) toggling reverts regression in our dev harness. Hypothesis: reorder + KV cache eviction race.

2026-03-10 13:40 UTC — Priya Desai (SRE): Opened temporary mitigation: disabled microbatch reordering in Hosted canary (10% traffic) and in Dedicated pool-3. Early Canary results: TTFT restored to baseline for canary.

2026-03-10 15:22 UTC — Miguel Santos: Prepared rollback-hotfix branch (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime PR#1248) which disables the kernel reordering and reverts the quantized-kernel preference. Running integration tests on multi-region testbed.

2026-03-11 02:33 UTC — Customer Success (Liam O'Neill): Noted that private deployment customers require an out-of-band patch for on-prem nodes; working with Solutions to schedule rolling patch windows.

2026-03-11 09:10 UTC — Engineering (Miguel): Canary in Hosted expanded to 40% after green metrics. Dedicated pool-3 hotfix applied; observed tokens/sec increase ~22% and TTFT drop by ~1.8s median. Continuing canary to 80% before full rollout.
2026-03-12 04:50 UTC — Design (Nora Li): Provided guidance for customer comms - status page blurb and in-product banner draft.

2026-03-12 18:00 UTC — Miguel Santos: Full rollback deployed to Hosted and Dedicated. Private on-prem customers received RPM and patch instructions; two customers scheduled maintenance windows for 2026-03-14. Monitoring shows metrics returning to baseline, but one Dedicated pool still intermittently spikes — tracking separately (ENG-8477).

2026-03-13 10:36 UTC — Aisha Kumar: Post-mortem kickoff scheduled. Action items: add e2e regression tests for reorder+kv-cache combinations, add more observability around KV cache warm/rewarm latency, and tighten canary criteria to include TTFT percentiles.
postmortem_notes: Root cause: race between new microbatch reordering scheduler and prefix/KV cache invalidation that caused a path into a non-cached rewarm that serialized on P2 CPU locks; compounding factor: quantized-kernel preference introduced a cross-device sync that on some drivers caused stalls. Fix: rollback reorder heuristic and quantized preference, add fine-grained KV-cache lockless checks and increase cache TTL for long-lived sessions. Long term: replace heuristic reordering with workload-aware policy, add synthetic e2e tests simulating mixed long/short-turn chat, and implement kernel handshake timeout metrics.
